name: Jamaica
summary: A gold saltire dividing the field into green triangles at top and bottom and black triangles at hoist and fly. Raised at independence on 6 August 1962, it is the only national flag without red, white or blue.
origin: A bipartisan parliamentary committee designed the flag in 1962 for independence from the United Kingdom, drawing on public suggestions.
The committee's first proposal had horizontal stripes, but it was found to resemble Tanganyika's flag, so the design was changed to a saltire. The flag was first raised at midnight on 6 August 1962.

symbols.name: Saltire
symbols.description: A gold diagonal cross from corner to corner.
symbols.meaning: The diagonal cross recalls the Saltire of St Andrew; no official religious meaning is attached.

history.label: Colony of Jamaica
history.note: Blue ensign with the colonial badge.

facts: The official meaning was revised in 1996: originally black stood for 'hardships overcome and to be faced'.
The national motto, 'Out of Many, One People', appears on the coat of arms, not the flag.
It is the only current national flag that has none of red, white or blue.
clues: A gold diagonal cross with green triangles top and bottom and black triangles at the sides.
The only national flag with no red, white or blue.
An earlier horizontal design was dropped for looking like an East African flag.
Its black triangles were once said to represent hardships.
